subject: AWS Private Offer renewal — seat reallocation, consumption credits, and invoice mapping
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara@medicore.health>
To: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@medicore.health
Date: Wed, 10 Jul 2024 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal questions + seat/top-up before PO

Hi Aditya,

We’re getting our renewal committee together and have a couple of practical asks before we issue a PO through AWS Private Offer:

- We want to bump committed capacity ~25% for the next 12 months (spike expected in Q4). Can that be split between our US and EU business units on a single private offer?
- How do consumption credits show up on the Marketplace invoices? We need separate EU invoices for VAT reclaim.
- Any way to apply existing credits we have from your last quarter pilot against the renewal?

Can you loop in whoever handles Marketplace billing mapping? We’d like a short note back this week so we can coordinate procurement + legal.

Thanks,
Tara
Director, Cloud Platforms
Medicore Health
[Attachment: procurement-rfi-2024-07.pdf (pdf)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@medicore.health>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2024 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal questions + seat/top-up before PO

Tara — thanks for the note and context. High level answers below; Marissa/Laura will drop the invoice mapping and legal flow.

1) Seat/commit split: yes — we can allocate the committed capacity across business units in the AWS private offer. Practically we’ll create a primary PO that covers the total committed $ and then add a line-level allocation: "US: 70% / EU: 30%" which your procurement team can use for internal chargebacks.

2) Credits & invoices: consumption credits are passed through Marketplace as line-item offsets. For EU VAT, we can request split invoices (one for the EU portion) — there is an extra step in the private offer acceptance that AWS needs to apply. Laura will outline that flow.

3) Existing credits: if those credits are on our account (RDW account credits), we can apply them against the first tranche of the renewed PO; if they live on AWS Marketplace (credit code), we’ll need to coordinate with AWS to map the code to the new private offer.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa to provide a sample invoice export and the exact private-offer acceptance checklist for EU split invoicing.
- Laura to confirm DocuSign timeline for the PO and any legal redlines to watch for.
- I’ll draft a short mutual action plan and send back by EOD Friday.

Attached: Redwood PO SOW (v3) — outlines committed units, billing cadence, and SLA notes.

Gracefully,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_AWS_PO_SOW_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@medicore.health>, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2024 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal questions + seat/top-up before PO

Hi Tara — looping in the Marketplace ops side. A few operational notes and a sample file attached.

- Invoice mapping: we can emit two invoice streams from our side for the same private offer by using line-item tagging. AWS then produces separate invoices; your procurement team will get one file for US and one for EU. See sample export attached.
- Credits: attached is how a credit line looks on the Marketplace CSV (credit code + offset). If the credit is on your AWS account, we just include the credit token on acceptance and AWS applies it.
- Timing: once DocuSign is completed, AWS typically needs 3–5 business days to finalize the PO acceptance and generate the first invoice.

Checklist for you:
1) Confirm split allocation percentage (we assumed 70/30 in Aditya’s note).
2) Confirm legal signatory and procurement contact for DocuSign.
3) Confirm whether the existing credit is an RDW-issued credit or AWS marketplace credit token.

I’ve attached an example CSV of the AWS marketplace invoice so your accounting can validate.

Marissa Cole
Sales Operations — Redwood Marketplace
[Attachment: aws-po-invoice-example.csv (csv)]

From: Tara Singh <tara@medicore.health>
To: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@medicore.health, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2024 11:17:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Renewal questions + seat/top-up before PO

Thanks — helpful. A couple clarifications from procurement/legal:

- We confirm the 70/30 split (US/EU).
- We will need separate invoices for VAT reclaim; please move forward with the acceptance checklist you mentioned.
- The credit we referenced is an AWS marketplace credit token (we have a code). I’ll share the token with procurement once we have the DocuSign sent so we don’t expose it in email.

Open question: can we reallocate seats mid-term if usage trends differently (i.e., shift more of the commit to US mid-12mo)? Any fees or amendment process? Also need to confirm SLA credit terms in the SOW — our Legal flagged a request for a 99.9% monthly uptime target and an explicit SLA credit schedule.

If you can send a short mutual action plan with dates (DocuSign send, expected AWS acceptance, invoice issuance), we’ll route PO and the credit token.

Best,
Tara

Date: Wed, 24 Jul 2024 15:37:00 -0700
Subject: RE: AWS Private Offer renewal — seat reallocation, consumption credits, and invoice mapping

Tara — thanks for the confirmations. Below is the mutual action plan (MAP) and a short answers list to the mid-term reallocation and SLA ask.

Mutual Action Plan (timeline):
- 07/24: RDW sends DocuSign (PO + SOW) — signatory: Ana Patel (Medicore Procurement)
- 07/26: Medicore returns signed DocuSign + provides AWS credit token to procurement@redwoodinference.com
- 07/30: RDW submits acceptance package to AWS Marketplace (requesting split invoices: US/EU)
- 08/02–08/06: AWS acceptance window (3–5 business days) — first invoice generation and formal PO number issuance

Mid-term reallocation: allowed. Process: submit a seat reallocation amendment (internal form) with 30 days’ notice; if the total committed $ remains the same we’ll reassign line-item percentages free of charge once per 6-month period. Any increase to committed $ mid-term will be handled as an amendment (pro-rated invoice).

SLA: We can commit to 99.9% monthly uptime for production inference endpoints. SLA credits: 5% credit of monthly invoice for each SLA tier missed (capped at 30% per month). Legal can include the explicit schedule in the SOW appendix.

Next steps (what I’ll do now):
- Send DocuSign package with PO + SOW v3 and the SLA appendix (attached to DocuSign).
- Marissa will upload the invoice export sample and instructions into the HubSpot deal.
- Laura will add the AWS acceptance checklist to the DocuSign note so your procurement knows what AWS requires for split invoicing.

If anything else is required to speed this, please let me know — otherwise we’ll proceed with the MAP above.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: DocuSign_Redwood-Medicore_PO.pdf (pdf)]
